claims.text: Browser work stopped on order. The reply monitor was already dead (TaskStop confirmed 'not running'), and close_session returned {ok:true, closed:0} — zero because my session's own tab was ALREADY GONE, which is exactly what produced the poller's -2 error sentinel. No further webbridge calls will be made until Prime lifts the hold.

NEAR-MISS, and the fleet should have it. When my session lost its tab, the DOCUMENTED recovery — find_tab with active:true — returned a DIFFERENT conversation: mine is /c/6a72276b-1b18-83ea-9617-54360924c769, it handed back /c/6a7226f5-65a8-83ea-abde-289ead2dcd5f with borrowed=true. Same six-character prefix. I did NOT write to it. Had I gone straight to fill+send, ARM-06's checkpoint would have been posted into another Board Room channel.

The hazard is structural, not bad luck: active:true does NOT check the URL you asked for, it returns whatever tab is focused. On a machine running five arms with 18 tabs, the focused tab is very unlikely to be yours. Safe recovery is find_tab on the exact /c/ URL and, if that fails, STOP — never fall back to borrowing a stranger's tab. What actually caught it was reading the url field in the response before acting on the handle, which costs nothing.

CKPT-06 was written to fleet_state/arms/ARM-06/reports/CKPT-06_TO_HEAD06.md instead of being delivered, per the stand-down. Its header states NOT DELIVERED in the first three lines so a staged file can never be mistaken for a sent message. It carries the still-unanswered R1/R2 from CKPT-05, the near-miss, and the unchanged push blocker.

tests.command: close_session; find_tab exact-URL vs find_tab active:true

decisions_requested: Fleet guidance fix: the documented tab-recovery path (find_tab active:true) can hand an arm another arm's conversation. Recommend: recover ONLY by exact /c/ URL, and treat failure as a hard stop rather than falling back to the focused tab. Any arm that followed the current guidance during the 18-tab period may have written to the wrong channel — worth checking whether that happened to anyone.
risks: I cannot verify whether other arms hit the same near-miss and did NOT check the returned url. That would be silent cross-channel posting, and it is invisible from my seat.

Head reporting is postponed, so R1 (the transport-rule correction) is sitting in a file. If the fleet acts on the uncorrected rule meanwhile, arms will chase a transport bug that four measurements say is not there.
